title: Triage decisions — state/triage.json
description: Output of prompts/02_triage_rules.md, written once after intake. Consumed by prompts/03 (KPI-tree seeding from the playbook's signature_kpis), tools/compute_kpis.py (--playbook), tools/compute_ratios.py (--family), prompts/31 (which sector pack AND tier-2 playbook to read) and prompts/41 (which standard exhibit set to draw from). Until 2026-08-03 this shape was consumed by four modules and validated by nothing, so a triage file could omit the playbook slug and every downstream consumer would silently degrade.

sector.description: T2 classification. The family/playbook pair is the routing contract; both must resolve against config/sector_registry.yaml, which tools/validate_state.py checks.

playbook.description: A playbooks.* slug from config/sector_registry.yaml, or null when no sub-sector matched. As of 2026-08-03 all 32 playbooks are status: authored, so null should be rare and means the classifier found nothing — not that the playbook is unwritten.

playbook_status.description: Mirrors the registry entry's status at classification time. `pending` means triage degraded to the family pack; no registry entry currently uses it.

confidence.description: high = >=3 distinct registry keywords all pointing to one playbook; medium = 1-2 keywords, or matches across two playbooks in one family; low = no keyword match, or matches spanning two families. Record `low` honestly — a confidently wrong classification routes the whole run down the wrong KPI tree.

matched_keywords.description: The registry keywords that actually matched. Evidence for the confidence score.

rejected_alternatives.description: Playbooks considered and rejected, each with a reason. Makes the classification inspectable rather than asserted.

secondary_playbooks.description: Multi-segment companies: playbooks of the non-primary segments. Deep research applies the primary fully and pulls only the KPI table from these.

bfsi_statements.description: Set from families.<family>.bfsi_statements. True switches extraction to the BFSI addendum in prompts/10 and makes compute_ratios.py suppress families.bfsi.skip_ratios.

generic_reason.description: Required in spirit when playbook == 'generic': which of the three situations landed here, per prompts/sector_playbooks/generic.md. Collapsing them is the main way a generic run produces a weak note.

recheck.description: T2-RECHECK: the mandatory re-classification after module 03 writes state/business_model.json. If it disagrees with the first pass, the recheck is adopted and the KPI tree is marked stale.

data_mode.description: T7. `sparse` routes through prompts/70_sparse_data_playbook.md, which matters more in sparse mode, not less.

research_order.description: T3 scheduling: the order DR1/DR2 and the analysis waves were planned in. The order may vary per company; the reason it varied must be traceable (CLAUDE.md rule 4).

decisions.description: One entry per triage rule fired. This is the audit trail that makes 'dynamic, not a flow' explainable — every branch records what it examined and why it chose.

rule.description: Rule id from prompts/02, e.g. T1, T2, T7, or T2-RECHECK.
